prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: 1024x1024 seamless flat base-color/albedo texture for a rotating 3D asteroid in a hand-drawn 2.5D game. Image 1 is the current asteroid brush albedo and is the EDIT TARGET and exact surface-paint style reference. Image 2 is the approved five-family CONCEPT REFERENCE only, use the corresponding row's material identity, never its lighting or black outlines. Repaint image 1 into this material family: Copper-bearing asteroid. About 60 percent medium iron slate-grey paint, 25 percent broad muted russet/copper mineral plates, 15 percent restrained matte turquoise/verdigris pigment. Several broad intersecting mineral bands with irregular chipped paint boundaries. Copper is a pigment color, not shiny metal. Sparse blue-green mineral deposits must be broad enough to read at small scale. No orange illumination.
Preserve the original texture's broad directional gouache brushwork, asymmetrical interlocking mineral regions and deliberately quiet planes. Around 6 to 10 large regions across the sheet. All surface detail should survive when a whole asteroid is only 80 pixels wide. Flat color only, no directional shading, no cast shadows, no ambient occlusion, no black creases, no holes, no outlines, no white specular highlights, no crater motifs. No dense grunge, speckles, tiny facets, triangulated low-poly mosaic or noisy hatching. A separate authored mesh provides recesses, graphite drawing and lighting. The result must be a tileable flat texture filling the entire square canvas, not a rock render, not a material ball, not a swatch sheet. No margins, text, background scene or UI. Keep all four edges tileable.
